Placement volatility of each person-year

Source: R/plcvol.R
plcvol.Rd

Counts how often a person's placement region changes within a period (a fiscal year), from records that each carry the region at the time of placement ra and the region of the most recent placement rb. For a person-year with records r = 1, ..., R in a given order the count is $$v = \sum_r 1(A_r \ne B_r) + \sum_{r > 1} 1(A_r \ne A_{r-1}),$$ a change within a record (within) plus a change between consecutive records (across), as Ruhela (2026) defines placement volatility for Ontario's restrictive confinement records (Appendix H).

Usage

plcvol(ra, rb, id, ord = c("region", "given"))

Arguments

ra, rb

The region at the time of placement and the region of the most recent placement of each record: labels (text, factors or numbers), compared as text.

id

The person-year of each record: one label, or a list of labels (person and year) combined.

ord

"region" or "given", the order of the records within a person-year.

Value

A data frame of class plcvol, one row per person-year in the order of first appearance: id (the labels, one column each when id is a list), n (records), within, across and vm (their sum).

Details

The first sum does not depend on the order of the records, the second does. A release without placement dates fixes no order, so ord says which is used: "region" sorts each person-year's records by ra (the order of the published analysis code), under which across is the number of distinct regions at placement less one and no longer depends on how the rows arrived; "given" keeps the rows in the order given. See proof("plcvol"): 0 <= v <= 2R - 1, with equality possible; v = 0 when every record stays in one region; the count is unchanged by an injective relabelling of the regions and can fall when two regions are merged.

Rows missing id, ra or rb are dropped. The work is one ordering of the rows, O(n log n) for n rows, then one pass.

References

Ruhela, V. S. (2026). Alert complexity and placement volatility in Ontario restrictive confinement data. Major research paper, Centre for Criminology and Sociolegal Studies, University of Toronto.

Examples

ra <- c("East", "East", "West", "North", "North")
rb <- c("East", "West", "West", "North", "East")
plcvol(ra, rb, id = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2))
#> plcvol: 2 person-years, records in region order; mean volatility 1.5 (within 1, across 0.5)
#>  id n within across vm
#>   1 3      1      1  2
#>   2 2      1      0  1
plcvol(ra, rb, id = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2), ord = "given")
#> plcvol: 2 person-years, records in given order; mean volatility 1.5 (within 1, across 0.5)
#>  id n within across vm
#>   1 3      1      1  2
#>   2 2      1      0  1
